validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, FERC-certificated project. FERC Docket CP20-484-000: ANR Pipeline Company filed an NGA section 7(c) application June 22, 2020 for the 'Alberta Xpress Project' -- one new greenfield compressor station (Turkey Creek Compressor Station, 15,900 hp) plus a mainline valve modification in Evangeline Parish, Louisiana, and a capacity lease with Great Lakes Gas Transmission (GLGT) for 165,000 Dth/d ($81.1M) -- confirmed by two independent Federal Register notices (notice of application 2020-14663; notice of availability of the final EIS 2021-24106), TC Energy's own project fact sheet, TC Energy's FY2022 SEC 6-K ('Placed the Alberta XPress project in service in January 2023'), and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (Applied/Construction/Completed history, same $81.1M/165 MMcf/d/Jan-2023-in-service). SCOPE: this is a compression-only expansion (one new compressor station; the FEIS's '36-inch suction/discharge piping' is internal station piping, not mainline pipe) -- LengthKnown=0 km and blank Diameter are CORRECT per the expansion-with-no-new-physical-pipe rule, not an omission. DUPLICATE CHECK (cross-row context): confirmed P2501 (Alberta Xpress Expansion Project, Michigan->Louisiana, 0 km, $81.1M, 165 MMcf/d, in-service Jan 2023) and P5547 (Wisconsin Reliability Project, in the parallel A7/west batch, Wisconsin->Wisconsin, 48 mi of new pipeline replacing 51 mi of old pipe, 150 MMcf/d/144,000 Dth/d, in-service 2025) are two distinct, non-overlapping ANR expansion projects under the same parent 'ANR Gas Pipeline' pipeline_name -- confirmed by TC Energy's own Wisconsin Reliability Project page (entirely different scope, geography, capacity and timeline). NOT a duplicate; no action needed on either PID.
